name: Tracheal Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Tracheal Agenesis

criteria.description: Complete absence or discontinuity of the tracheal lumen confirmed by endoscopy or imaging
Severe respiratory distress and inability to intubate the trachea at birth
Abnormal bronchial anatomy such as bronchi arising directly from the esophagus
Presence of associated congenital anomalies (e.g., cardiac, gastrointestinal)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or discontinuous tracheal lumen with respiratory distress and characteristic bronchial anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed postmortem due to the fatal nature of the condition.

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing severe hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis
imaging: Chest X-ray showing absent tracheal shadow
CT or MRI demonstrating absence or discontinuity of trachea
Bronchoscopy confirming absent tracheal lumen and abnormal bronchial anatomy
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic cases reported
Possible association with VACTERL and other syndromic anomalies
other: Postmortem examination confirms diagnosis in most cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of tracheal lumen with dynamic collapse rather than complete absence
Symptoms may improve with supportive care
Obstruction at the level of the larynx rather than absence of trachea
May present with similar respiratory distress but different anatomical findings
Presence of trachea with abnormal connection to esophagus
Usually trachea is present and patent

redFlags: Immediate severe respiratory distress at birth
Failure to intubate or ventilate the neonate
references: Feldman KW, et al. Tracheal agenesis: a review of the literature and report of two cases. Pediatr Pulmonol. 1991.
Smith LP, et al. Congenital tracheal anomalies: diagnosis and management. Chest Surg Clin N Am. 2003.
